p.src: (MARGARET on FAUST’S arm. MARTHA and MEPHISTOPHELES walking up and down.)

u.src: MARTHA and MEPHISTOPHELES walking up and down.)

p.src: I feel, the gentleman allows for me, Demeans himself, and shames me by it; A traveller is so used to be Kindly content with any diet. I know too well that my poor gossip can Ne’er entertain such an experienced man.

u.src: I feel, the gentleman allows for me, Demeans himself, and shames me by it; A traveller is so used to be Kindly content with any diet.
I know too well that my poor gossip can Ne’er entertain such an experienced man.

p.src: A look from thee, a word, more entertains Than all the lore of wisest brains.

u.src: A look from thee, a word, more entertains Than all the lore of wisest brains.

p.src: Don’t incommode yourself! How could you ever kiss it! It is so ugly, rough to see! What work I do,—how hard and steady is it! Mother is much too close with me.

u.src: How could you ever kiss it!
It is so ugly, rough to see!
What work I do,—how hard and steady is it!
Mother is much too close with me.

p.src: And you, Sir, travel always, do you not?

u.src: And you, Sir, travel always, do you not?

p.src: Alas, that trade and duty us so harry! With what a pang one leaves so many a spot, And dares not even now and then to tarry!

u.src: Alas, that trade and duty us so harry!
With what a pang one leaves so many a spot, And dares not even now and then to tarry!

p.src: In young, wild years it suits your ways, This round and round the world in freedom sweeping; But then come on the evil days, And so, as bachelor, into his grave a-creeping, None ever found a thing to praise.

u.src: In young, wild years it suits your ways, This round and round the world in freedom sweeping; But then come on the evil days, And so, as bachelor, into his grave a-creeping, None ever found a thing to praise.

p.src: I dread to see how such a fate advances.

u.src: I dread to see how such a fate advances.

p.src: Then, worthy Sir, improve betimes your chances!

u.src: Then, worthy Sir, improve betimes your chances!

p.src: Yes, out of sight is out of mind! Your courtesy an easy grace is; But you have friends in other places, And sensibler than I, you’ll find.

u.src: Yes, out of sight is out of mind!
Your courtesy an easy grace is; But you have friends in other places, And sensibler than I, you’ll find.

p.src: Trust me, dear heart! what men call sensible Is oft mere vanity and narrowness.

u.src: Trust me, dear heart! what men call sensible Is oft mere vanity and narrowness.

p.src: Ah, that simplicity and innocence ne’er know Themselves, their holy value, and their spell! That meekness, lowliness, the highest graces Which Nature portions out so lovingly—

u.src: Ah, that simplicity and innocence ne’er know Themselves, their holy value, and their spell!
That meekness, lowliness, the highest graces Which Nature portions out so lovingly—

p.src: So you but think a moment’s space on me, All times I’ll have to think on you, all places!

u.src: So you but think a moment’s space on me, All times I’ll have to think on you, all places!

p.src: Yes, for our household small has grown, Yet must be cared for, you will own. We have no maid: I do the knitting, sewing, sweeping, The cooking, early work and late, in fact; And mother, in her notions of housekeeping, Is so exact! Not that she needs so much to keep expenses down: We, more than others, might take comfort, rather: A nice estate was left us by my father, A house, a little garden near the town. But now my days have less of noise and hurry; My brother is a soldier, My little sister’s dead. True, with the child a troubled life I led, Yet I would take again, and willing, all the worry, So very dear was she.

Not that she needs so much to keep expenses down: We, more than others, might take comfort, rather: A nice estate was left us by my father, A house, a little garden near the town.
But now my days have less of noise and hurry; My brother is a soldier, My little sister’s dead.
True, with the child a troubled life I led, Yet I would take again, and willing, all the worry, So very dear was she.

p.src: I brought it up, and it was fond of me. Father had died before it saw the light, And mother’s case seemed hopeless quite, So weak and miserable she lay; And she recovered, then, so slowly, day by day. She could not think, herself, of giving The poor wee thing its natural living; And so I nursed it all alone With milk and water: ’twas my own. Lulled in my lap with many a song, It smiled, and tumbled, and grew strong.

u.src: I brought it up, and it was fond of me.
Father had died before it saw the light, And mother’s case seemed hopeless quite, So weak and miserable she lay; And she recovered, then, so slowly, day by day.
She could not think, herself, of giving The poor wee thing its natural living; And so I nursed it all alone With milk and water: ’twas my own.
Lulled in my lap with many a song, It smiled, and tumbled, and grew strong.

p.src: The purest bliss was surely then thy dower.

u.src: The purest bliss was surely then thy dower.

p.src: But surely, also, many a weary hour. I kept the baby’s cradle near My bed at night: if ’t even stirred, I’d guess it, And waking, hear. And I must nurse it, warm beside me press it, And oft, to quiet it, my bed forsake, And dandling back and forth the restless creature take, Then at the wash-tub stand, at morning’s break; And then the marketing and kitchen-tending, Day after day, the same thing, never-ending. One’s spirits, Sir, are thus not always good, But then one learns to relish rest and food.

u.src: But surely, also, many a weary hour.

p.src: Yes, the poor women are bad off, ’tis true: A stubborn bachelor there’s no converting.

u.src: Yes, the poor women are bad off, ’tis true: A stubborn bachelor there’s no converting.

p.src: It but depends upon the like of you, And I should turn to better ways than flirting.

u.src: It but depends upon the like of you, And I should turn to better ways than flirting.

p.src: Speak plainly, Sir, have you no one detected? Has not your heart been anywhere subjected?

u.src: Speak plainly, Sir, have you no one detected?
Has not your heart been anywhere subjected?

p.src: The proverb says: One’s own warm hearth And a good wife, are gold and jewels worth.

u.src: The proverb says: One’s own warm hearth And a good wife, are gold and jewels worth.

p.src: I mean, have you not felt desire, though ne’er so slightly?

u.src: I mean, have you not felt desire, though ne’er so slightly?

p.src: I’ve everywhere, in fact, been entertained politely.

u.src: I’ve everywhere, in fact, been entertained politely.

p.src: I meant to say, were you not touched in earnest, ever?

u.src: I meant to say, were you not touched in earnest, ever?

p.src: One should allow one’s self to jest with ladies never.

u.src: One should allow one’s self to jest with ladies never.

p.src: I’m sorry I’m so blind: But I am sure—that you are very kind.

u.src: I’m sorry I’m so blind: But I am sure—that you are very kind.

p.src: And me, thou angel! didst thou recognize, As through the garden-gate I came?

u.src: And me, thou angel! didst thou recognize, As through the garden-gate I came?

p.src: Did you not see it? I cast down my eyes.
And thou forgiv’st my freedom, and the blame To my impertinence befitting, As the Cathedral thou wert quitting?

u.src: And thou forgiv’st my freedom, and the blame To my impertinence befitting, As the Cathedral thou wert quitting?

p.src: I was confused, the like ne’er happened me; No one could ever speak to my discredit. Ah, thought I, in my conduct has he read it— Something immodest or unseemly free? He seemed to have the sudden feeling That with this wench ’twere very easy dealing. I will confess, I knew not what appeal On your behalf, here, in my bosom grew; But I was angry with myself, to feel That I could not be angrier with you.

p.src: (She plucks a star-flower, and pulls off the leaves, one after the other.)

u.src: (She plucks a star-flower, and pulls off the leaves, one after the other.)

p.src: No, it is just in play.

u.src: No, it is just in play.

p.src: (She pulls off the leaves and murmurs.)

u.src: (She pulls off the leaves and murmurs.)

p.src: Loves me—not—loves me—not— (plucking the last leaf, she cries with frank delight:)

u.src: Loves me—not—loves me—not— (plucking the last leaf, she cries with frank delight:)

p.src: Yes, child! and let this blossom-word For thee be speech divine! He loves thee! Ah, know’st thou what it means? He loves thee!

u.src: Yes, child! and let this blossom-word For thee be speech divine!
Ah, know’st thou what it means?

p.src: O tremble not! but let this look, Let this warm clasp of hands declare thee What is unspeakable! To yield one wholly, and to feel a rapture In yielding, that must be eternal! Eternal!—for the end would be despair. No, no,—no ending! no ending!

u.src: O tremble not! but let this look, Let this warm clasp of hands declare thee What is unspeakable!
To yield one wholly, and to feel a rapture In yielding, that must be eternal!
Eternal!—for the end would be despair.

p.src: I’d ask you, longer here to tarry, But evil tongues in this town have full play. It’s as if nobody had nothing to fetch and carry, Nor other labor, But spying all the doings of one’s neighbor: And one becomes the talk, do whatsoe’er one may. Where is our couple now?

p.src: He seems of her still fonder.

u.src: He seems of her still fonder.

p.src: And she of him. So runs the world away!
